notes: This source/test traceability contract covers the bounded IEEE 1516.1-2025 Unpublish Object Class Directed Interactions service in Umbra's opt-in, non-installable development profile. The official C++ binding exposes the §5.7 service through a whole-class overload and an interaction-class-set overload. The focused production-filesystem regression verifies that undefined object or interaction class inputs append no successful-void report; the interaction-set overload appends ObjectClassHandle type 36 and supplied InteractionClassHandleSet type 28; a supplied empty set remains type 28 with an empty Array<InteractionClassHandle>; and the whole-class overload retains that same optional argument position as type-34 Null. Every record is appended after its accepted registry transition. The Requirements Lab assigns the coalesced §5.7 source candidates to clause-5.7.4; RL-078 records that source-ownership mismatch while this contract retains the direct §5.7 source context. Table 5's rotated InteractionClassHandleSet row has no row-level Requirements Lab candidate (RL-067/RL-076); its exact Array<InteractionClassHandle> form and the static MIM type-28 enumerator are retained in implementation comments and focused source/API traceability. Complete directed delivery matrices, subscriptions, timestamped/retraction behavior, DDM, public MOM delivery, remote transport, packaging, validation, and conformance remain outside this slice.
